description: Compiler & VM Refactoring — eliminate structural duplication in compiler.c and vm.c before the syntax redesign lands

userStories.title: Consolidate global arity lookups
userStories.description: As a developer working on the compiler, I want a single function for looking up global arity information so that I don't have to maintain four near-identical linear scans.
acceptanceCriteria: Four functions replaced with a single `compiler__find_global(c, name)` returning `GlobalArity*`: remove compiler__resolve_global_arity (lines 1225-1235), compiler__resolve_global_info (lines 1237-1248), compiler__resolve_global_type (lines 1250-1259); rename/keep compiler__find_global_arity (lines 1261-1270) as the single entry point
All call sites updated to use the single function and access GlobalArity fields directly
No callers do their own root-walk or linear scan — all go through the single function
All existing tests pass
Compiler builds cleanly with no new warnings
userStories.notes: GlobalArity struct is defined at compiler.c lines 569-579 with fields: name, known_arity, is_mutable, suspends, captures_mutable, type, struct_type_idx, return_type, param_types. Callers currently extract individual fields via separate functions — just return the pointer and let them access fields directly.

userStories.title: Merge CPS argument extraction
userStories.description: As a developer working on CPS transforms, I want the shared extraction logic in one place so that adding new CPS-aware constructs doesn't require duplicating 100 lines.
acceptanceCriteria: A shared helper extracted that takes an AstNode** array of arguments, identifies which ones are suspending, generates synthetic [def __aN ...] AST nodes for each, and returns the modified argument array plus the synthetic defs
compiler__compile_cps_extract_args (lines 2245-2344) becomes a thin wrapper calling the shared helper
compiler__compile_cps_extract_def_value (lines 2346-2436) becomes a thin wrapper calling the shared helper
The shared helper covers: temp name generation, ast_alloc sequence, var ref / name node / def head / def command construction
All existing tests pass, especially any CPS/suspension-related tests
userStories.notes: The two functions differ only in where the modified node gets inserted into the new statement list — one modifies a command's arguments, the other modifies a def's value expression. The core loop (lines 2269-2322 vs 2369-2416) is structurally identical: same temp name generation, same ast_alloc sequence, same var ref / name node / def head / def command construction.

userStories.title: Extract HOF builtin compilation helper
userStories.description: As a developer adding new higher-order builtins (like for, par-each), I want a shared compilation helper so each new builtin is ~5 lines instead of ~40.
acceptanceCriteria: A compiler__compile_hof_builtin helper extracted with signature like: (Compiler* c, const char* name, uint32_t name_len, AstNode** args, uint32_t argc, uint8_t opcode, uint32_t line, uint32_t col)

The helper handles: arity check (exactly 2 args), non-suspending callback validation (local slot check, global arity check, block suspension point check), collection compilation, in_non_suspending_callback save/set/restore, callback compilation, opcode emission
transform builtin (lines 4103-4141) rewritten as one call to the helper
each builtin (lines 4143-4181) rewritten as one call to the helper
filter builtin (lines 4183-4221) rewritten as one call to the helper
All existing tests pass
userStories.notes: The three builtins share identical 30-line non-suspending callback validation blocks. The only differences are the builtin name (for error messages) and the final opcode. The in_non_suspending_callback flag needs careful save/restore — the current code does this and the helper must preserve the pattern.

userStories.title: Extract shared struct field marshaling
userStories.description: As a developer, I want struct field read/write logic defined once so that changes to type marshaling don't require updating six copy-pasted switch statements.
acceptanceCriteria: embed__struct_read_field (embed.c lines 836-873) promoted to a shared function accessible by both vm.c and embed.c
embed__struct_write_field (embed.c lines 876-919) promoted to a shared function accessible by both vm.c and embed.c
OP_STRUCT_GET (vm.c lines 3924-3987) calls the shared read function instead of inlining the type switch
OP_STRUCT_SET (vm.c lines 3989-4054) calls the shared write function instead of inlining the type switch
OP_STRUCT_GET_DYN (vm.c lines 4056-4105) calls the shared read function
OP_STRUCT_SET_DYN (vm.c lines 4107-4160) calls the shared write function
Static vs dynamic opcode variants differ only in how they resolve field offset and type — marshaling is shared
Shared functions placed wherever makes sense (value.c, shared header as static inline, etc.) and included in unity build if new file
All existing tests pass, including embed API tests
userStories.notes: The embed.c functions already work as standalone functions that take (struct_data, offset, field_type, heap/val) and do the type-switch marshaling. Promote these rather than writing new ones. They always box through JaclVal — the static opcodes lose a minor 'mixed boxing' optimization for i64/u64/f64 but this is negligible for a scripting language and can be revisited if profiling shows it matters.

userStories.title: Macro-ify typed arithmetic opcodes
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the 20 typed arithmetic/comparison opcode handlers generated by macros so the pattern is obvious and mechanical changes don't risk introducing bugs in one of 20 copies.
acceptanceCriteria: VM__I64_BINOP(op) macro defined that handles: pop two values, cast to int64_t, apply operator, push result, break
VM__F64_BINOP(op) macro defined that handles: pop two values, memcpy to double, apply operator, memcpy back or box as bool, push, break
Extended variants for div/mod that include zero-check before the operation
Unary neg variants handled (either separate macro or parameterized)
i64 opcodes (lines 3338-3463) replaced with macro invocations: ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, MOD, NEG, LT, GT, LE, GE, EQ
f64 opcodes (lines 3465-3627) replaced with macro invocations: ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, MOD, NEG, LT, GT, LE, GE
Macros defined near their usage in vm.c (not in a shared header — they are vm-internal)
Arithmetic macros do not change evaluation order (pop b first, then a) or error behavior (div/mod zero checks)
All existing tests pass
userStories.notes: Use do { ... } while(0) or statement-expression patterns for macro hygiene. Comparison ops for f64 return bool (jacl_bool) not f64 — the macro may need a variant or parameter for this. The i64 comparison ops also return bool.
